cancer_indication: Advanced or metastatic hormone receptor–positive (HR+) breast cancer (typically HER2–), especially after progression on other endocrine therapy.
moa: Fulvestrant competitively binds estrogen receptor α (ERα), blocking estrogen binding and triggering receptor ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. As a pure antiestrogen with no agonist activity, it causes complete shutdown of ER signaling. In ER+ breast cancer cells, this leads to G1 cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis. Its clinical effect is often combined with targeted agents such as CDK4/6 inhibitors or a PI3K inhibitor for synergistic benefit.

GOBP_ESTROGEN_RECEPTOR_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: Estrogen receptor–driven signaling and transcriptional programs mediated by ERα (ESR1) (and to a lesser extent ERβ/ESR2) that promote luminal breast cancer growth.
GOBP_ESTROGEN_RECEPTOR_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation:
ER-driven transcription is the core dependency in HR+ breast cancer that fulvestrant targets by degrading ERα and shutting down estrogen-responsive gene expression.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Tumors that depend on active ER signaling are more likely to respond to ER degradation by fulvestrant; if ER signaling is already low/down, the tumor is less ER-dependent and fulvestrant is less likely to produce benefit. (PubMed Central)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High ER/estrogen-response dependency in ER+ breast cancer predicts benefit from ER downregulation/antagonism with fulvestrant.
FDA label (FASLODEX) (FDA Access Data); DrugBank: DB00947 (DrugBank); ChEMBL: CHEMBL1358 (EMBL-EBI); PMID:27908454 (FALCON) (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: ER pathway can remain transcriptionally “high” yet be functionally bypassed by ESR1 activating alterations or growth-factor crosstalk, yielding relative endocrine resistance.
PMID:16113098 (NFκB/endocrine resistance context) (PubMed); PMID:21501600 (SERD/ER turnover) (PubMed); PMID:4009946 (ESR1 mutations; PMC) (Europe PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Bulk ER signaling may look “down” due to sampling/heterogeneity, yet residual ER-addicted clones can still respond to fulvestrant.
PMID:26178788 (sequential biopsies on fulvestrant) (PubMed); PMID:28680952 (fulvestrant review) (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low/absent ER signaling (ER-low/ER− phenotype) implies minimal drug target engagement → primary resistance.
FDA label (ER-driven indication) (FDA Access Data); PMID:28680952 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Fulvestrant competitively antagonizes ER and promotes ER protein downregulation, suppressing ER-driven transcription and proliferation.
FDA label MOA (FDA Access Data); DrugBank DB00947 (DrugBank); PMID:21501600 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even with ER signaling suppressed, tumors can persist via ER-independent RTK/PI3K/MAPK or cell-cycle bypass programs.
PMID:7572750 (PI3K/endocrine resistance review; PMC) (PMC); PMID:8379900 (HER2/endocrine resistance review; PMC) (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Fulvestrant cannot increase functional ER signaling; any “up” signature would reflect composition effects (e.g., more ER+ cells detected) rather than true activation under drug.
FDA label MOA (FDA Access Data); PMID:28680952 (PubMed)

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: PI3K–AKT–mTOR growth and survival signaling that can be hyperactivated in HR+ breast cancer (e.g., via PIK3CA mutations).
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation:
This pathway provides pro-survival signaling and reduced dependence on ER signaling, contributing to endocrine resistance in breast cancer.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Activating PIK3CA/PI3K–AKT signaling promotes cell survival and mediates endocrine (including fulvestrant) resistance; combining PI3K inhibitors with fulvestrant shows clinical benefit in PIK3CA-mutant disease. (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some ER+ tumors have PI3K pathway activation yet remain ER-dependent enough that ER degradation still yields response (often improved with combination strategies).
PMID:7572750 (PI3K in HR+ BC; PMC) (PMC); PMID:7388095 (PI3K/ER crosstalk review; PMC) (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: PI3K/AKT/mTOR hyperactivation supports ligand-independent survival/proliferation and is a major endocrine-resistance axis in ER+ breast cancer.
PMID:7572750 (PMC); PMID:7388095 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low PI3K/AKT/mTOR survival signaling is more consistent with “pure” ER addiction, favoring fulvestrant sensitivity.
PMID:28680952 (fulvestrant review) (PubMed); PMID:7572750 (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Endocrine resistance can arise despite low PI3K signaling (e.g., ESR1 alterations, RB/E2F bypass, or other RTKs).
PMID:3204388 (ER/E2F axis; PMC) (PMC); PMID:4009946 (ESR1 mutations; PMC) (Europe PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In responders, ER shutdown can reduce ER-driven growth-factor programs and downstream PI3K survival tone, supporting tumor control.
PMID:26178788 (biopsy signaling changes on fulvestrant) (PubMed); PMID:7572750 (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even if PI3K signaling falls, tumors may persist via MAPK, NFκB, or cell-cycle escape.
PMID:16113098 (PubMed); PMID:8379900 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Transient feedback PI3K activation after ER blockade may occur but still be insufficient to prevent response in strongly ER-addicted disease.
PMID:7572750 (PMC); PMID:7388095 (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Adaptive RTK→PI3K/AKT/mTOR upregulation is a canonical escape route after endocrine pressure, driving acquired resistance.
PMID:7572750 (PMC); PMID:12109706 (endocrine resistance overview; PMC) (PMC)

KEGG_ERBB_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: ErbB/HER family receptor signaling (including HER2/ERBB2, ERBB3, ERBB4, and EGFR) that can drive proliferation and survival.
KEGG_ERBB_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation:
Growth factor receptor signaling can bypass ER blockade; ERBB-family upregulation is described as a resistance mechanism in the setting of endocrine blockade.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Upregulated HER family signaling provides bypass survival/proliferation signals and can be induced after ER blockade (fulvestrant can increase ErbB3/HER2 expression), producing resistance unless co-targeted. (PubMed Central)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Mild ERBB signaling can coexist with ER dependence (e.g., HER2-low/EGFR-low), allowing fulvestrant activity despite some RTK tone.
PMID:8379900 (HER2 & endocrine resistance; PMC) (PMC); PMID:28680952 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Strong EGFR/HER2 (ERBB) signaling can bypass ER control, a well-described mechanism of endocrine resistance.
PMID:8379900 (PMC); PMID:9254309 (HER2/endocrine resistance; PMC) (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low ERBB pathway activity supports an ER-driven luminal biology, favoring fulvestrant response.
PMID:27908454 (FALCON) (PubMed); PMID:28680952 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: ERBB-low tumors can still be resistant via ESR1 mutations, NFκB survival signaling, or RB loss.
PMID:4009946 (ESR1 mutations; PMC) (Europe PMC); PMID:16113098 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In responders, ER downregulation can reduce ER-driven expression of growth factors/RTK ligands, lowering ERBB pathway output.
PMID:26178788 (PubMed); PMID:28680952 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Despite low ERBB output, alternative pathways (PI3K/MAPK/NFκB) can maintain growth.
PMID:7572750 (PMC); PMID:16113098 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some tumors show compensatory ERBB upshift yet remain controlled if ER remains the dominant driver and ERBB activation is modest.
PMID:9254309 (PMC); PMID:28680952 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Adaptive EGFR/HER2 signaling after ER blockade is a classic acquired-resistance mechanism to endocrine therapy.
PMID:8379900 (PMC); PMID:9254309 (PMC)

KEGG_MAPK_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: MAPK/ERK signaling downstream of growth factor receptors that sustains proliferative signaling.
KEGG_MAPK_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation:
MAPK/ERK activity can maintain proliferation and is described as increased in fulvestrant-resistant contexts.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- ERK pathway activation sustains proliferation and can circumvent ER loss; ERK activation correlates with fulvestrant resistance and combining ERK/MEK inhibition can restore sensitivity in models. (PubMed Central)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: MAPK activity can be elevated yet still subordinate to ER; fulvestrant can work if ER remains essential for the proliferative program.
PMID:6712962 (endocrine resistance pathways; PMC) (Europe PMC); PMID:28680952 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK signaling phosphorylates ER/co-activators and drives ER-independent proliferation → endocrine resistance.
PMID:6712962 (Europe PMC); PMID:599586 (Frontiers endocrine resistance review) (Frontiers)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low MAPK escape signaling supports ER addiction and endocrine sensitivity.
PMID:27908454 (PubMed); PMID:28680952 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Resistance can still occur via PI3K/mTOR, RB/E2F bypass, or ESR1 alterations even if MAPK is not dominant.
PMID:3204388 (PMC); PMID:7572750 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In responders, proliferation shutdown reduces growth-factor demand and downstream MAPK signaling output.
PMID:26178788 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even with MAPK low, tumors may survive through PI3K/NFκB anti-apoptotic signaling.
PMID:7572750 (PMC); PMID:16113098 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: A compensatory MAPK rise may be observed early yet not prevent response if ER blockade remains effective and MAPK induction is limited.
PMID:599586 (Frontiers)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: MAPK upregulation is a common adaptive bypass after endocrine therapy, sustaining proliferation despite ER suppression.
PMID:599586 (Frontiers); PMID:6712962 (Europe PMC)

BIOCARTA_NFKB_PATHWAY.description: NF-κB survival signaling that drives anti-apoptotic gene expression in tumor cells.
BIOCARTA_NFKB_PATHWAY.interpretation:
Active NF-κB is associated with survival/resistance, while its suppression is described as important for fulvestrant-induced apoptosis.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- NF-κB drives expression of anti-apoptotic/pro-survival genes (e.g., BCL2 family); IRF1 induction suppresses NF-κB and promotes fulvestrant-induced apoptosis — active NF-κB therefore promotes resistance. (PubMed Central)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some immune-infiltrated ER+ tumors may show NFκB/IFN programs that increase death signaling (e.g., IRF1 axis), supporting endocrine response.
PMID:2925293 (IFNγ restores fulvestrant sensitivity; PMC) (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Constitutive NFκB promotes anti-apoptotic survival and has long been linked to endocrine resistance in ER+ breast cancer.
PMID:16113098 (PubMed); PMID:15657351 (NFκB inhibitor restores fulvestrant apoptosis) (PubMed); PMID:32013374 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low NFκB pro-survival signaling reduces an anti-apoptotic barrier, favoring fulvestrant-induced growth arrest/apoptosis.
PMID:15657351 (PubMed); PMID:28680952 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Tumors can be NFκB-low yet resistant via PI3K/MAPK bypass or RB/E2F deregulation.
PMID:7572750 (PMC); PMID:3204388 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Effective endocrine control can reduce inflammatory signaling and secondarily dampen NFκB pathway output.
PMID:7792133 (endocrine therapy immunomodulation; PMC) (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: NFκB may fall while resistance persists through other survival axes (PI3K/MAPK) or cell-cycle escape.
PMID:7572750 (PMC); PMID:6712962 (Europe PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Treatment-triggered immune activation can increase NFκB signatures (immune-cell composition) without implying tumor-cell survival dominance.
PMID:7792133 (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: NFκB-driven anti-apoptotic adaptation can blunt fulvestrant-induced apoptosis; NFκB inhibition restores ICI 182,780 apoptosis in resistant cells.
PMID:15657351 (PubMed); PMID:32013374 (PubMed)

REACTOME_GPER1_SIGNALING.description: GPER1 (GPR30) signaling as an alternate membrane estrogen receptor pathway that can persist during fulvestrant treatment.
REACTOME_GPER1_SIGNALING.interpretation:
Loss of GPER1 signaling is described as associated with fulvestrant resistance; GPER1-mediated signaling may represent a potential resistance route during treatment.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Repression/loss of GPER1 has been linked experimentally to fulvestrant resistance (GPER modulation and epigenetic changes observed in resistant cell models). (PubMed Central)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some tumors with GPER signaling still respond if classical nuclear ER signaling is the primary driver and dominates phenotype.
PMID:28680952 (PubMed); PMID:30646517 (GPER in BC; EuropePMC) (Europe PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: GPER activation is implicated in endocrine resistance; antiestrogens (including fulvestrant) can act as GPER agonists, supporting pro-growth signaling in some contexts.
PMID:30646517 (Europe PMC); PMID:32973677 (GPER & antiestrogens; EuropePMC) (Europe PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low GPER signaling reduces a potential non-genomic estrogen escape route, improving likelihood of fulvestrant benefit in ER-driven disease.
PMID:32973677 (Europe PMC); PMID:28680952 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: GPER-low tumors may still be resistant via PI3K/ERBB/MAPK bypass or RB/E2F deregulation.
PMID:7572750 (PMC); PMID:8379900 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (direct): Fulvestrant is not a GPER antagonist; any observed decrease in GPER signaling would be indirect (e.g., expression changes), not direct pharmacology.
PMID:30646517 (Europe PMC); PMID:32973677 (Europe PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: If GPER signaling drops but disease progresses, resistance is likely mediated by other axes (ERBB/PI3K/MAPK).
PMID:8379900 (PMC); PMID:7572750 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Fulvestrant can act as a GPER agonist, but ER degradation may still dominate and yield response if GPER signaling is weak/limited.
PMID:30646517 (Europe PMC); DrugBank DB00947 (DrugBank)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Fulvestrant-associated adaptation can involve GPER dysregulation; GPER activity may promote endocrine-resistant phenotypes and correlate with fulvestrant resistance mechanisms.
PMID:24169358 (FUL resistance + GPER/CDK6) (PubMed); PMID:32973677 (Europe PMC)

GOBP_CELL_CYCLE_G1_S_PHASE_TRANSITION.description: Regulatory processes controlling G1 cell-cycle arrest and progression through the G1/S checkpoint, including Cyclin D–CDK4/6 and RB/E2F control noted in the source.
GOBP_CELL_CYCLE_G1_S_PHASE_TRANSITION.interpretation:
Fulvestrant efficacy is linked to inducing G1 arrest; upregulation of G1/S drivers (e.g., Cyclin D/CDK6 activity) is described as a mechanism that can overcome ER blockade.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Upregulation of CDK6 (and/or cyclin D/CDK4/6 axis) enables G1→S progression despite ER loss; high CDK6 correlates with shorter PFS on fulvestrant and combining CDK4/6 inhibitors with fulvestrant is effective clinically. (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Highly proliferative ER+ tumors can still respond if proliferation remains ER-driven (often less durable without addressing CDK4/6).
PMID:26178788 (fulvestrant biopsies; Ki67 context) (PubMed); PMID:28680952 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: High G1/S drive (e.g., CDK6 up, RB pathway bypass) predicts endocrine resistance and shorter PFS on fulvestrant.
PMID:27252418 (CDK6 predicts resistance to fulvestrant) (PubMed); PMID:3204388 (ER/E2F axis; PMC) (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low proliferation (luminal A-like) is classically more endocrine sensitive, consistent with fulvestrant benefit.
PMID:27908454 (PubMed); PMID:26178788 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Low proliferation does not preclude resistance if ER is non-functional or if survival pathways (PI3K/NFκB) dominate.
PMID:7572750 (PMC); PMID:32013374 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: ER degradation reduces cyclin D/E2F programs and induces G1 arrest, lowering G1/S transition activity in responders.
PMID:26178788 (PubMed); PMID:28680952 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Despite ER suppression, CDK6-mediated bypass or RB dysfunction can maintain cell-cycle progression and drive resistance.
PMID:27252418 (PubMed); PMID:3204388 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Fulvestrant does not directly promote G1/S progression in tumor cells; increased “G1/S” signatures under therapy generally reflect non-response or sampling/composition artifacts.
FDA label MOA (FDA Access Data); PMID:27252418 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Failure to suppress proliferation (persistent G1/S activity) indicates endocrine escape and clinical progression on fulvestrant.
PMID:27252418 (PubMed); PMID:26178788 (PubMed)

GOCC_RB_E2F_COMPLEX.description: RB/E2F control referenced as governing E2F target gene expression and the G1 checkpoint in breast cancer cells.
GOCC_RB_E2F_COMPLEX.interpretation:
RB1 loss/downregulation is described as abrogating fulvestrant-induced G1 arrest, enabling unchecked proliferation despite ER loss.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- RB1 loss abrogates the G1 checkpoint and undermines fulvestrant-induced G1 arrest; RB loss is associated with endocrine resistance. (PubMed Central)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Presence of an intact RB–E2F suppressive complex (functional RB control) supports endocrine sensitivity because ER-driven cyclin D/CDK4 dependence remains targetable.
PMID:3204388 (ER/E2F program; PMC) (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: RB can be intact yet tumors resist via ER-independent survival (PI3K/ERBB) or ESR1 alterations.
PMID:7572750 (PMC); PMID:4009946 (Europe PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some RB/E2F deregulation may exist, yet if ER remains dominant and RB loss is incomplete, fulvestrant can still produce partial control.
PMID:3204388 (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: RB pathway loss/dysfunction reduces reliance on ER→cyclin D control, enabling E2F-driven proliferation despite fulvestrant.
PMID:3204388 (PMC); PMID:27252418 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: By suppressing ER-driven cyclin D/CDK activity, fulvestrant promotes RB hypophosphorylation and RB–E2F binding, consistent with growth arrest and sensitivity.
PMID:3204388 (PMC); PMID:26178788 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even with RB–E2F binding, tumors may persist via anti-apoptotic signaling or parallel mitogenic pathways.
PMID:16113098 (PubMed); PMID:7572750 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: If tumor burden rapidly falls, bulk cycling/complex assembly signatures can contract despite sensitivity (composition effect).
PMID:7792133 (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Persistent loss of RB–E2F complex formation (RB loss or strong CDK bypass) aligns with fulvestrant resistance and ongoing proliferation.
PMID:27252418 (PubMed); PMID:3204388 (PMC)

REACTOME_INTERFERON_GAMMA_SIGNALING.description: IFNγ-driven signaling through STAT1 and IRF1 described as an immune/stress axis that can influence tumor apoptosis programs.
REACTOME_INTERFERON_GAMMA_SIGNALING.interpretation:
Activation of IFNγ–STAT1–IRF1 signaling is described as sensitizing breast cancer cells to fulvestrant by suppressing survival programs and promoting caspase-dependent apoptosis.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- IFNγ induces IRF1/STAT1 which suppresses NF-κB and anti-apoptotic BCL2 family members and promotes caspase activation — IRF1 activity restores fulvestrant sensitivity in resistant models. (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: IFNγ→STAT1/IRF1 programs can suppress NFκB and pro-survival BCL2-family signaling, restoring antiestrogen (fulvestrant) sensitivity in resistant breast cancer models.
PMID:2925293 (IFNγ restores fulvestrant sensitivity; PMC) (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (ER+ clinical context): High IFNγ signatures in ER+/HER2− can correlate with distinct biology and worse prognosis in some cohorts, potentially reflecting less endocrine-responsive disease.
PMID:7582264 (IFNγ prognosis in ER+HER2−; PMC) (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Many endocrine-sensitive luminal tumors are relatively “immune-cold”; low IFNγ signaling does not prevent fulvestrant benefit when ER dependence is high.
PMID:27908454 (PubMed); PMID:7792133 (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: IFNγ-low tumors can still be resistant due to tumor-intrinsic ER bypass (PI3K/ERBB/MAPK) rather than immune-state.
PMID:7572750 (PMC); PMID:8379900 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Endocrine therapy can modulate the tumor immune microenvironment and antigen-presentation/IFN programs, which may support tumor control in a subset of ER+ disease.
PMID:7792133 (endocrine therapy immunomodulation; PMC) (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: IFNγ signaling can coexist with immune-evasion programs or inflammation-associated progression; this is not a direct fulvestrant MOA and is typically context-dependent.
PMID:7582264 (PMC); PMID:7792133 (PMC)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: With tumor regression, immune infiltration and IFNγ signals can contract, lowering bulk IFNγ signatures despite sensitivity.
PMID:7792133 (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Persistently low IFNγ reflects an immune-desert state; progression on fulvestrant in this setting is usually driven by tumor-intrinsic resistance rather than IFNγ itself.
PMID:7792133 (PMC); PMID:7572750 (PMC)

REACTOME_APOPTOSIS.description: Apoptotic signaling described as caspase-dependent apoptosis activated as fulvestrant takes effect.
REACTOME_APOPTOSIS.interpretation:
Apoptosis pathway activation is described as enhancing fulvestrant antitumor effect, particularly in ER+ tumor cells.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Fulvestrant’s anti-tumor effect in ER+ cells involves induction of caspase-dependent apoptosis (IRF1/BAX/BAK mediated); active apoptotic machinery facilitates drug efficacy. (PubMed Central)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Baseline apoptotic priming increases likelihood that ER blockade triggers caspase-dependent death in ER-dependent breast cancer cells.
PMID:28680952 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Tumors can show apoptosis signaling yet evade death via strong anti-apoptotic programs (e.g., NFκB/BCL2 family), yielding resistance.
PMID:15657351 (PubMed); PMID:16113098 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Even with low baseline apoptosis, fulvestrant can induce apoptosis (or durable arrest) when ER dependence is high.
FDA label MOA (FDA Access Data); PMID:28680952 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Strong suppression of apoptosis via NFκB/pro-survival signaling is a hallmark of endocrine-resistant states and blunts fulvestrant cytotoxicity.
PMID:15657351 (PubMed); PMID:32013374 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In responders, fulvestrant-driven ER downregulation leads to growth arrest and can activate apoptotic programs in ER+ breast cancer tissue/cells.
PMID:26178788 (biopsy study) (PubMed); PMID:28680952 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Apoptosis genes may rise transiently, but anti-apoptotic escape (NFκB/BCL2) prevents execution, yielding resistant persistence.
PMID:15657351 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some endocrine responses are dominated by cytostatic quiescence/senescence rather than overt apoptosis, lowering bulk apoptosis signatures despite benefit.
PMID:26178788 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Failure to engage apoptosis under fulvestrant pressure (persistent survival signaling) aligns with non-response/progression.
PMID:15657351 (PubMed); PMID:7572750 (PMC)

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: High expression of ER target genes is described as indicating robust ER signaling, which predicts good fulvestrant response.
High expression of ER target genes is described as indicating robust ER signaling, which predicts good fulvestrant response.
IFNγ induces STAT1 as part of an IFNγ–STAT1–IRF1 axis described to restore fulvestrant sensitivity by promoting apoptotic signaling and suppressing survival programs.
IRF1 induction is described to suppress NF-κB/BCL2 and trigger caspase-dependent apoptosis, restoring fulvestrant sensitivity.
Upregulation of pro-apoptotic BAX is described as part of IFNγ-driven restoration of fulvestrant sensitivity through apoptosis.
Upregulation of pro-apoptotic BAK1 (BAK) is described as part of IFNγ-driven restoration of fulvestrant sensitivity through apoptosis.
Upregulation of caspase-dependent apoptosis (including caspase 8) is described as amplifying fulvestrant-induced cell death and enhancing drug effect.
Upregulation of caspase-dependent apoptosis (including caspase 9) is described as amplifying fulvestrant-induced cell death and enhancing drug effect.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Suppression of BCL2 (described as part of IFNγ/IRF1 effects) is linked to enabling caspase-dependent apoptosis and restoring fulvestrant sensitivity.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: PIK3CA mutations are described to hyperactivate PI3K–AKT–mTOR signaling, driving survival and reduced dependence on ER signaling, leading to fulvestrant resistance.
Upregulation/overexpression of HER2 (ERBB2) is described as a bypass mechanism that can render fulvestrant ineffective in resistant contexts.
ERBB3 expression is described as increased with endocrine blockade in ER+ contexts and as part of ErbB-family bypass signaling linked to fulvestrant resistance.
ERBB4 expression is described as increased with fulvestrant/endocrine blockade in ER+ contexts, contributing to compensatory ErbB signaling.
EGFR is described as part of ErbB-family signaling that can be upregulated and provide alternate mitogenic drive despite ER inhibition.
CDK6 overexpression is described to drive G1/S progression despite ER loss, mediating resistance to fulvestrant.
Cyclin D1 amplification/upregulation is described as a cell-cycle driver that can push cells through G1/S regardless of ER blockade, contributing to resistance.
Activating ESR1 mutations (e.g., Y537S, D538G) are described as emerging in endocrine-resistant metastatic tumors and reducing fulvestrant efficacy.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss/downregulation of GPER1 signaling is described as associated with fulvestrant resistance.
Loss of RB1 (E2F control) is described as abrogating fulvestrant-induced G1 arrest, permitting unchecked proliferation and resistance.
Downregulation of STAT1 is described as detrimental because STAT1 is part of IFNγ–STAT1–IRF1 signaling needed to trigger fulvestrant-induced apoptosis.
Downregulation of IRF1 is described as detrimental because IRF1 suppresses NF-κB/BCL2 and is required for caspase-dependent apoptosis linked to fulvestrant effect.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR+/HER2– (Luminal A/B): Clinical data confirm fulvestrant’s benefit is confined to ER+ (Luminal) tumors. In HR+/HER2– (Luminal A/B) metastatic cancer, fulvestrant demonstrates efficacy similar to aromatase inhibitors; the FALCON trial showed longer PFS with fulvestrant vs anastrozole in previously untreated HR+/HER2– cases.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-positive: HER2+ tumors (HER2-enriched or Luminal B with HER2 amplification) are often endocrine-resistant and typically require combined HER2 blockade; fulvestrant is not used as monotherapy in HER2+ disease.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Triple-negative/basal-like: Triple-negative/basal-like tumors (virtually all ER–) lack ERα and do not respond to fulvestrant.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.BRCA1/2-mutated or “HRD+”: BRCA1/2-mutated or “HRD+” cancers are treated with DNA-damage agents, not fulvestrant; only if they co-express ER would fulvestrant be considered.
